name: Stadtturm Innsbruck
kurzbeschreibung: The 51-metre-high Stadtturm in Innsbruck's Old Town: built in 1450, 133 steps to the viewing platform, watchman history, and onion dome.
beschreibung:
Overview

Rising to a height of 51 metres, the Gothic Stadtturm von Innsbruck stands prominently in the picturesque pedestrian precinct of Herzog-Friedrich-Straße in the heart of Innsbruck's historic old town. Built directly adjoining the Old City Hall and only steps away from the famed Goldene Dachl, the tower has embodied the civic confidence of the Tyrolean provincial capital since the mid-15th century. After ascending a historic spiral staircase, visitors on the open viewing platform at 31 metres are rewarded with a magnificent 360-degree panorama across the colourful gables of the old town, the Nordkette mountain range, and Patscherkofel.

Architectural History & Watchman Tradition

The Stadtturm was constructed between 1442 and 1450 adjoining the pre-existing town hall. While church and castle spires served ecclesiastical and aristocratic rulers, the city tower was the defensive symbol of an autonomous citizenry. For nearly five centuries, municipal tower watchmen (Türmer) carried out their vigilant duties around the clock: day and night they kept watch over the rooftops, sounding horn signals to sound the alarm against fires, spotting approaching hostile forces, and preserving order within the city. The lower section of the tower temporarily served as the municipal jail. The tower received its characteristic Renaissance onion dome with a lantern around 1560 under master builder Albrecht Mayr, after the original Gothic spire had become dilapidated. In 1586, the first mechanical tower clock was installed. To this day, the climb up the 133 stone and wooden steps of the gracefully curving spiral staircase attracts cultural travellers from all over the world.

Visit & Arrival

The Stadtturm is open daily all year round: during the summer months (June to September) daily from 10:00 to 20:00, and during the remaining months daily from 10:00 to 17:00. Admission prices (as of the 2025/2026 season): Adults approx. €4.50, reduced/seniors/students €3.50, children (6 to 15 years) €2.00, family ticket approx. €9.00. With the popular Innsbruck Card, entry is free. Arrival by public transport: From Innsbruck Hauptbahnhof on foot in about 10 minutes along Maria-Theresien-Straße directly into the old town; by tram (line 1 or 3) or city bus to the stop Maria-Theresien-Straße or Marktplatz. By car: Parking in Markthallen-Garage or Rathaus-Galerien-Garage.

Tips

Due to its historic architecture with a narrow, protected spiral staircase, the tower is not wheelchair accessible; good basic fitness and surefootedness are required for the 133 steps. Visit the observation platform in summer during the golden hour before sunset, when the warm evening light bathes the craggy peaks of the Nordkette in an alpine glow and reveals an unforgettable view down over the Goldene Dachl.
oeffnungszeiten: Täglich geöffnet: Juni–Sept 10:00–20:00 Uhr, sonst 10:00–17:00 Uhr
